title: Periods of 727 ASAS-3 Mira variables changed by 1.1 percent rms from 2000-2009 to 2013-2025 as random wander; early trends did not continue, and only NSV 08001 exceeded the wander
abstract: Question: do Mira variables show period changes over two decades that are larger than random period wander, as expected after a thermal pulse? We measured the periods of the 2,896 ACVS Mira stars in independent time windows of ASAS-3 (V, 2000-2009) and ASAS-SN Sky Patrol v2 (V and g, 2012-2025), with a cycle-jackknife error, and used Gaia DR3 long-period-variable periods as a third check. For 727 stars that pass strict quality and saturation cuts, the period change over 15.7 years has a robust scatter of 1.23 percent with a median error of 0.47 percent; a Gaussian excess of 1.19 percent rms fits the data (likelihood ratio 680), and the mean change is -0.10 percent. Inside ASAS-SN, adjacent windows 3.1-3.6 years apart agree with the errors, but windows 6.7 years apart show a 0.76 percent excess, so the periods wander with time. The 2001-2007 trend does not predict the 2015-2021 trend (322 stars, Spearman 0.05, p = 0.35), and the AAVSO rates of Templeton et al. (2005) do not predict the new changes for the 8 weak-case stars that pass our cuts (1 of 8 with the same sign). Against the wander model, 8 stars have |z| > 3 (2.0 expected); after Bonferroni correction only NSV 08001 (265.2 to 248.3 d, -6.6 percent, Gaia 252 +/- 10 d) remains as a fast-change candidate, and one other outlier (V1596 Sgr) is an ASAS-3 artifact. Four stars with consistent 3-5 percent changes (RY Hyi, V1055 Oph, NSV 09906, ASAS J054812-3200.1) are consistent with the wander. Limitations: southern sky only, 15.7-year baseline, saturated bright Miras (R Aql, R Hya) excluded, and residual wrong ASAS-3 periods for faint bulge stars.

display.caption: Period scatter beyond the jackknife measurement error versus the time between window centres. Green: ASAS-SN thirds (same survey); blue: ASAS-3 thirds; red: ASAS-3 third versus ASAS-SN third; black diamond: likelihood fit for the full ASAS-3 and ASAS-SN windows (727 stars). The dashed line is a random walk in ln P through the black point. Error bars are 68 percent bootstrap ranges over stars; a value at zero means no excess.

The ASAS-3 period trend from 2001 to 2007 (A1 to A2) against the ASAS-SN trend from 2015 to 2021 (B1 to B2) for 322 Miras. The four windows do not overlap. The dashed line shows full continuation of the early trend; the data show no relation.

Distribution of z = (period change) / (measurement error, jitter and 1.19 percent wander) for 727 Miras, with the expected Gaussian. Eight stars have |z| > 3 (2.0 expected); two have |z| > 4: V1596 Sgr (ASAS-3 artifact, at the right edge) and NSV 08001.

ASAS-SN photometry (Kochanek et al. 2017) gives the second epoch.
